design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. The member asks only for more time on a decision she believes is pending. Policy alone reveals a two-hop tree: the member-requested deadline extension waits on an undecided transition-of-care request (none is on file), and the units of that request wait on the expiry release of the ended intensive outpatient approval (never booked). Difficulty comes from reading the prerequisite sentences, checking the records hop by hop and reconciling three multi-factor computations over the unit ledger, the claim ledger, appeals, care management and primary care referrals; there is one tool per problem, so tool choice is not the difficulty.
SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4,6,6]; auth_ext_expiry_release takes 4, auth_ext_transition_units 6, auth_ext_member_review_extension 6. Occupied before: nothing (first task). Claimed: those three policies and tools release_expired_units_43b7942e, record_transition_of_care_request_bf098d50, request_review_time_extension_2522d00e. Left for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisites, [6,4,4,6]): the approved-authorization cluster (provider change, member extension request, extension) and the void of an overlapping approval, none of which this task touches.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root auth_ext_member_review_extension (user tool, the customer's own write). Edge 1: root -> auth_ext_transition_units, state_gate, gate auth_authorizations.request_origin, form state, sentence 'The days a member-requested deadline extension adds are not fixed until a transition-of-care request for the member stands on file undecided.' (negated direction; four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until', a record-visible state (a request of origin transition of care, undecided), no tool/id/code token, hard requirement). Only the transition-of-care write in this difficulty creates such a request. Seed: the only authorization is PA-2607-208814 with request_origin provider_request, status expired -> false at frozen_time. Edge 2: auth_ext_transition_units -> auth_ext_expiry_release, value_input, gate toc_released, form state, sentence 'The units a transition-of-care request asks for are fixed only after every earlier approval of the member for the same service code whose end date has passed carries an expiry release entry.' (affirmative direction; state = an expiry release entry on the ended approval; only the expiry-release write books entries with release reason expired, a void books 'voided' and applies to approvals still open). Seed: E0 end 2026-08-25, ledger grant 12 + 6 uses, no release -> false. Topological order: release (step 13) -> transition-of-care request (15) -> deadline extension (17). Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the release makes units_requested 14 instead of 15; skipping the request removes the request the extension is recorded on (compute raises; terminal rows missing). user_scenario names neither the release nor the request as a step. Tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).
DERIVATION FROM VISIBLE TEXT. The member asks for more time -> the deadline-extension rule says its days are not fixed until a transition-of-care request stands undecided -> find_auth_authorizations shows none -> the transition-of-care rule records such a request built on the earlier approval for the same service -> its sentence says its units wait on an expiry release entry on every ended approval for the service -> find_auth_units shows E0 ended without a release -> the expiry-release rule books it. Each hop admits one reading.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Release (subject auth_units_released): auth_void_withdraw has no structured gate (policy_scope); auth_validity_units' sentence 'Units left on end_date are released the next day ...' is overridden by the declared overwrite (hold-backs). Transition-of-care request (auth_submit): auth_agg_duplicate_request.no_open_duplicate - E0 (S9480) is expired, not submitted/pended/approved, so no open duplicate; auth_transition_of_care.toc_window - anchor plan_memberships.coverage_start_date 2026-07-08, 90 calendar days counted from the day after, inclusive, last day 2026-10-06; 2026-09-24 is day 78 (positive), 2026-10-07 would fail (negative); auth_agg_multi_holding, auth_out_of_network, auth_service_scope policy_scope. Deadline extension (auth_timeline_extension): auth_turnaround.extend_before_deadline - anchor the new request's received_date 2026-09-24, 7 calendar days from the day after, inclusive -> last day 2026-10-01; taken the same day (positive), 2026-10-02 would fail. The deadline may be extended once: no earlier extension exists on the new request.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target of the release: E0 (authorization_id key); rows aggregated: its grant (12) and 6 posted uses; excluded: nothing else on E0. The two denied program-day claims (08-10 duplicate_claim under provider appeal AG-2608-01947, 08-11 no_prior_authorization) are not posted uses; they are why units are held back. Target of the transition-of-care request: new row copying E0's class, providers and service code (source_authorization_id = E0 carried on the call). Target of the extension: the new request (authorization_id from the step-15 receipt).
FACTOR CARD (world facts at handling time; baselines from the Step 5 sensitivity run). Expiry release (standard 6, fall-back 6, result 1): claims_lag_holdback method - 30 days after end, weeks 4, pace 1.5 -> 1 (baseline 0 -> 2); reprocessing_holdback - C26-0811-62431 denied no_prior_authorization 2026-08-11 -> 1 (-> 2); appeal_holdback - AG-2608-01947 under_review, claim_denial -> 1 (-> 2); discharge_session_holdback (multi-source) - Complex Case Management active AND follow-up 2026-08-17 -> 2 (-> 3). Near-miss: the 08-10 claim is denied too but for duplicate_claim, which the reprocessing hold-back does not count (it is the appeal hold-back's claim). Transition-of-care request (standard 9 after release, fall-back 9, result 15): hospital_stay_credit method multi-source - inpatient C26-0812-70056 paid AND follow-up -> weekly cap 5 (-> 10); late_request_cut - day 78 -> 4 (-> 19); step_down_addition multi-source - Complex CM AND care plan update 2026-08-28 -> 3 (-> 12); population_addition - ABD Care -> 2 (-> 13); attendance_cut - 6/12 -> 1 (-> 16); referral_addition - single referral RF-2608-40582 -> 1 (-> 14). Near-miss: the care assessment of 2026-08-21 is not a care plan update. Deadline extension (fall-back 13, result 5): gathering_days multi-source - Complex CM AND contact 2026-09-15 -> 5 (-> 10); mailing_days method - mail -> 5 (-> 3); transition_window_cut - day 78 -> 3 (-> 8); referral_cut - single -> 1 (-> 6); appeal_addition - claim-denial appeal only -> 1 (-> 4); risk_cut - 3.41 -> 2 (-> 7). Cross-difficulty evidence seeded: plan membership and claims, appeal case, care episode and activities, PCP assignment and referral.
SEED ROWS. customers (identity), plan_memberships (category, coverage start, notice channel), auth_authorizations E0 (the ended approval; its missing release is the load-bearing open state), auth_units (grant + 6 uses: the reconciliation), auth_actions (approval and adverse determination notices of the partial approval), plan_claims (two denied program days + inpatient stay), appeal_cases (open claim-denial appeal), care_enrollments + care_activities (tier, risk, follow-up, plan update, contact), pcp_assignments + pcp_events (single referral). Removing any factor's evidence moves its tier to the fall-through and changes the result (sensitivity figures above). Automatic clauses checked: no approval is active, so no expiry or concurrent review fires; the appeal is under review with due date 2026-10-08 (not past); no premium or renewal obligation is lit.
PERSONA. A tired, apologetic first-person voice; volunteers the phone number, her situation and the ask for more time; gives Medicaid ID, date of birth, SSN last four, ZIP, program and old plan only when asked; cannot give the prior plan's approval number, days left or codes; agrees passively to closing out the old approval and to putting something on file once the agent explains; runs the handed-over extension with exactly the reference and days the agent gives; ends when told the time is on record. It asks nothing no policy decides.
STANDARD SOLUTION. Reads 0-11 (locate by phone, verify with Medicaid ID + DOB, membership, authorizations, units, actions, claims, appeals, care episode, care activities, PCP assignment, PCP events). Step 13 release_expired_units_43b7942e(E0, 1). Step 15 record_transition_of_care_request_bf098d50(customer, membership, E0, 'S9480', 15). Step 17 (user) request_review_time_extension_2522d00e(new request id, 5).
VERIFICATION. Scratch harness (t0_eval.py) replays gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each policy with check_compute's own build_env/eval_compute on the handling-time world: REL 1 (singles 2/2/2/3, fall-back 6); TOC 15 (singles 10/19/12/13/16/14, fall-back 9; without the release 14); REXT 5 (singles 10/3/8/6/4/7, fall-back 13). Gate commands and outputs are recorded in the difficulty worklog.md.
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Using only the policy prose, the tool schemas, the lookups and the persona lines, the same three writes and values follow: the release sentence set lists four hold-backs with record conditions, each resolved by one lookup; the request's six adjustments and the extension's six components likewise. No second reading was found: the late-request cut and transition-window cut both count days from the coverage start date to the handling day (78), the within-month windows count dates less than the stated whole months before 2026-09-24.
REVISION ROUND 2 (policy-task audit round 1). F-1: the declared replacement of the base transition-of-care clause now quotes the standard-method sentence together with the six-adjustment sentence ('As the standard method, ... Six adjustments are added to or subtracted from that standard figure ...'), so the merged base and extended texts give the transition-of-care units one value. O-1: the standard figure is capped at the class's most units per approval in compute as the rule states (not binding here: 9 of 20). O-2: the expiry rule now states that an approval whose end date has passed owes the expiry release whatever its status shows, including one whose expiry was recorded without a release entry, which is this seed's state. O-3: the void rule applies only before the end date. O-8: care and appeal factors are no longer labelled cross-difficulty; plan and pcp factors keep it. The opening line's reference to continuing under the old plan's approval is the root rule's own scope and names no filing (audit observation 3 kept). Scored values unchanged; gates re-run.
OWNER NOTE. The blueprint names withdrawal as the member's own write; withdrawal has no computed parameter, so this task's customer write is the deadline extension 'when the member asks for it' (auth_turnaround), recorded with requested_by member and carried out by the member in person.
user_scenario:
You are Marisela Quintanar-Voss, sixty-two, living on your own outside Kearney. You talk plainly, a little tired, and you apologise when you ramble. You joined Prairie Ridge this summer after leaving Heartland Community Health Plan. You go to the intensive outpatient program at Cedar Bluff Behavioral Health; you stopped going for a while in August when you ended up in the hospital, and you want to get back to it. Last week the program's intake coordinator told you that, because you are still new to Prairie Ridge, you could keep going under the approval Heartland had given you, but that Prairie Ridge would need Heartland's approval number for that. You don't have it: you called Heartland and they are mailing you a copy of the approval letter, which should arrive in a week or so. You are calling because you are afraid it will be decided before you can send the number, and that it will go against you. You open with something close to: "Hi, this is Marisela Quintanar-Voss, my phone number is 4025520417. My program at Cedar Bluff says Prairie Ridge needs my old plan's approval number to decide on continuing my program days under my old plan's approval, and I don't have it yet, Heartland is mailing it. Can I get more time so it doesn't get turned down?"
You give your details only when the agent asks for them: your Medicaid ID is PR24719386, your date of birth is February 11, 1964 (1964-02-11), the last four of your Social Security number are 2638, and your ZIP code is 68847. If the agent asks which program, it is the intensive outpatient program at Cedar Bluff Behavioral Health; if asked about your old plan, it was Heartland Community Health Plan. You do not know any service codes, how many program days are left, or the exact day your Prairie Ridge coverage began (you think it was early July); you say the program or the agent would know better than you. You do not have Heartland's approval number, only the promise that the letter is in the mail, and you say so if asked. You still want to go back to the program.
You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever has to be done on your records for this. If the agent explains that your earlier Prairie Ridge approval for the program has ended and something about its unused days has to be closed out, you say that is fine, you are not using that one any more. If the agent says something has to be put on file first so your program days can continue under your old plan's approval, you say yes, please go ahead. You do not know how the extra time is worked out; if the agent asks how many days you want, you say you don't know how it works and whatever the rules allow for you is fine. If the agent tells you that you have to ask for the extra time yourself and hands that step to you with the request reference and the number of days, you do it right then with exactly what the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you get. If a number of days is quoted, you accept it. Once the agent tells you the extra time is on record, you thank them and say goodbye.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (release -> transition-of-care request -> deadline extension); no problem has two prerequisites, so there is no parallel pair to reorder. Each hop is forced: the extension needs the request to exist and the request's units read the release.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without step 15 there is no undecided transition-of-care request: the deadline extension has no request to be recorded on (the computation raises on the missing request), and the terminal state lacks the new auth_authorizations row and the extension/notice rows attached to it.
Skipping step 13 leaves toc_released 0: units_requested falls from 15 to 14 (standard figure 8 instead of 9), and the release row is missing from the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names releasing unused units, an expiry release, or recording a transition-of-care request as a step; the customer only asks for more time on a decision she believes is pending. Her agreement to close out the old approval and to put something on file are passive replies that fire only after the agent explains them.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: record_transition_of_care_request_bf098d50 creates the request whatever the state of the ended approval, and request_review_time_extension_2522d00e records an extension on any reference given; release_expired_units_43b7942e checks nothing. None of the three returns an error or a hint when a prerequisite is unmet (task_tools.py function bodies contain no condition on status, dates or ledger).
